Blackheath Prep is an outstanding school located in South East London. We offer an exceptional education that is well-balanced across the academic subjects, sport and the arts, in addition to a superb extra-curricular offer, supportive pastoral care, and wraparound care that meets the needs of busy parents. Our facilities include a purpose-built Science lab, IT and DT block, Library, Gym, 2.5 acre sports field as well as three Forest Schools, providing ample space for our pupils to roam and have mini-adventures. Our Nursery, extensively refurbished in 2025, offers a wonderfully spacious and creatively designed setting for our youngest pupils. Take a look here.
By the time they leave us in Year 6 our pupils have achieved outstanding results in their 11+ and secure outstanding senior school offers from the leading independent and grammar schools in London and Kent. Over 70% of our Year 6 leavers receive one or more scholarship offers from their schools of choice.
As part of the Eltham College Family of Schools, our pupils also benefit from a priority application process for those who select Eltham College as their senior school of choice.
Be part of the Blackheath Prep adventure!
Applications are now open for entry in 2027 – Nursery (January and September starts) and Prep (7+ and occasional vacancies).

ISI Inspection Report 2016
The ISI inspection framework is approved by the Department for Education. Schools undergo a scheduled inspection broadly every three years. Inspections report on a school’s compliance with the Independent School Standards Regulations, and where applicable the National Minimum Standards for Boarding Schools and the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS). Inspections result in a binary judgement of ‘met’ or ‘not met’ against each applicable standard. Safeguarding, welfare, and health and safety are a priority in all inspections.
“I’m delighted with the outstanding feedback from the ISI inspectors during their recent inspection. They were rigorous and meticulous in their inspection, looking at every aspect of the curriculum, school culture, safeguarding, leadership and governance. They canvassed opinions from pupils and parents, interviewed staff and Governors, observed lessons and playtimes, and in the process gained a deep understanding and appreciation of daily life at Blackheath Prep. They rightly recognised the richness and diversity of the curriculum, the culture of kindness and respect, the robust and effective leadership of the school, and the high academic standards achieved by pupils.” Guy Sanderson, Headmaster and CEO, Eltham College Family of Schools.

We know that choosing a school for your child is a very important decision and we are delighted that you are considering Blackheath Prep for your child’s education. Nursery is where their adventure begins at Blackheath Prep and is the main entry point for children joining our school. We do not have an intake at Reception for children aged 4+.

Our superb Nursery was completely re-furbished in Summer 2025 and offers three wonderfully spacious classrooms and well-equipped outdoor play areas for our youngest pupils to enjoy. Creatively designed, it offers a wonderful early years setting, using natural materials and neutral colour palettes to create a calm and relaxing space for our young pupils to play, learn and explore. Weekly trips to the our on-site Forest Schools encourages our youngest pupils to have fun in the great outdoors, discover nature close-up and have mini-adventures!
In Nursery, we nurture the children’s natural curiosity, creativity and critical thinking through fun, play- based tasks across a full school day.
We strive to offer a lively, fun and inspiring learning environment in which children have the freedom to express their own uniqueness and form positive relationships with others. We support children in making sense of their world through both child-initiated and adult-led learning opportunities, in an environment where they feel safe and cared for.
Play is at the heart of our provision, as it is our belief that children need to be actively involved in meaningful learning experiences. Play encourages them to practise and build on skills, work collaboratively with others, explore, observe, experiment and solve problems. It enables children to learn in a stimulating and interactive environment that is secure and safe, yet challenging.
No two Nursery days are alike, as the structure alters to accommodate additional activities, such as Forest School and specialist lessons including French, Drama, Dance, PE and Music. Our qualified and highly experienced staff will ensure activities are suited to your child’s unique needs and interests and help to build on their personal, social, physical and intellectual development, through both carefully planned provision and adult-led activities.

Our History
Take a step back in time and discover 200 years of history of our school.
In 1823, the Rev. W. Greenlaw founded a Christian boys’ boarding school in the building that is home to Blackheath Prep today. Later known as Christ’s College, the boarding school largely attracted the sons of servicemen and professionals working in Africa, Asia and America. It was subsequently privately owned by a succession of Headmasters until it became a charitable trust in the 1950s.
In the 1990s, a selective co-educational nursery and pre-prep was opened at the school and quickly became hugely popular with local families. As demand for places at the nursery grew, interest in Christ’s College dwindled and by 1998 the governors deemed the boarding school financially unviable. After 175 years as a boys’ boarding school, Christ’s College finally closed its doors.
In 1998, the nursery school was joined by a new prep school and both went from strength to strength. Refurbishment of the older buildings and the addition of new ones took place, including a multi-purpose hall in 2006 and a new dining hall and music suite in 2007.
In 2011, the school was formally renamed Blackheath Preparatory School. The original chapel at Christ’s College’s was converted into a library and, in 2015, a state-of-the-art art, design and technology block was added.
In September 2020, Blackheath Preparatory School welcomed Alex Matthews as Head. In 2021, under his leadership, the school began a period of transformation including a new name – Blackheath Prep – and the introduction of a new school crest.
In 2023 the school celebrated 200 years with a year-long programme of special events and commissions to mark the school’s long history of educating children in the local area. Watch a short video with highlights of how we celebrated our bicentenary.
In September 2023, Blackheath Prep entered a new chapter in the school’s history when it became part of the Eltham College Family of Schools. Find out more.
In September 2025, Vikki Lloyd joined Blackheath Prep as the new Head, succeeding Alex Matthews’ after his highly successful 5-year tenure.

Vision & Values
Our Vision
To offer an education without boundaries, giving every child the freedom to shine and achieve their full potential, upholding academic excellence, sparking curiosity and a joyful love of learning, nurturing kindness and wellbeing, and creating a strong sense of community.
Our Mission
We are committed to giving every child the opportunity to achieve their full potential and the courage to strive for excellence in all their endeavours. Through innovative and inspiring teaching and a rich and varied curriculum, we aim to spark children’s natural curiosity and sense of fun and adventure and to nurture a joyful love of learning.Community is at the very heart of our school, and kindness, appreciation, collaboration and contribution are values that we work hard to put into practice each day. We encourage every child to make the most of their time here so when they complete their journey with us they are ready for the next stage of their education and have the foundation for a successful, happy and fulfilled life.
Our Values
We have seven core values that guide our thinking and our behaviour. Each value is outlined in more detail to form our aims.
KindnessWe aim to be an inclusive, diverse, friendly and welcoming school, where kindness, compassion, courtesy and respect are paramount. We are generous and considerate towards others and take care of each other and ourselves. We help children learn how to put the powerful potential of kind words and deeds into action.
CuriosityWe aim to spark children’s natural curiosity for the world, leading them to discover, to wonder, to dare to go further. With their attention captivated, children think more deeply, ask more inquisitive questions and pursue their learning to new levels.
FreedomWe aim to give children freedom to grow, to push boundaries, to exceed their own expectations and ours. Our superb outdoor space provides wonderful scope for exploration and exhilaration. Our independent status allows us to be an innovative school that nurtures creative thinkers and risk takers.
AmbitionWe aim to be ambitious in the goals we set, striving to ensure that every child shines and reaches their full potential. Our Community
PTFA
Blackheath Prep’s Parents, Teachers and Friends Association (PTFA) plays a vital role in building positive links between home, the school and our local community. PTFA volunteers work hard all year round to enrich the social aspects of our school through a varied programme of events. They also raise funds for school activities and our partner charities.
A varied programme of events take place throughout the year, ranging from the popular Christmas and summer fairs, discos, ice-cream sales and playground tea parties to the evening socials for parents and the annual quiz night. The PTFA’S fundraising efforts have raised money for many different projects and in recent years have funded two adventure playgrounds at school as well as musical instruments for our Strings, Wind and Brass programmes. Most recently, the PTFA funded the development of our Garden of Imagination used by pupils for Forest School activities and the purchase of playground games sets.
Charity in our Community
Blackheath Prep is committed to supporting charitable endeavours in our local community and abroad. We actively encourage our pupils to think about their community, and the world at large. We help them to develop an appreciation of the advantages they have and an understanding of and empathy for those who may not be as fortunate. We also encourage support from our parents.
At Blackheath Prep, we place great value on building ongoing partnerships with smaller charities, and those in our local area. Throughout the year, we host a wide range of pupil-led fundraising and charitable initiatives in school, including Christmas jumper days, sponsored events, and table sales. The PTFA also raises money for a variety of charities and makes regular uniform donations to two schools in Zimbabwe.
For 2025/26, our chosen charities, as voted for by our pupils, are Emmie’s Books and Guide Dogs. Across the year, our pupils and families will participate in a wide range of fundraising activities to support these charities.
Local Charities we have supported
We regularly support the work of Lewisham-based MammaKind with donations of children’s clothes, toiletries and baby food.
The 999 Club in Deptford work with people experiencing homelessness and are one of our long-standing charity partners. We support their work with food donations from our harvest festival, and fundraising to buy new sleeping bags and other necessary items.
Greenwich Wildlife Network
One of our chosen charities voted for by pupils in 2024/25, we raised money and collected donations to support the work of this local charity.

Blackheath Prep is an outstanding, co-educational prep school for children aged 3 to 11. Our five-acre site offers superb specialist facilities, and plenty of space to provide our pupils with the freedom to learn and play in our large playgrounds, forest school areas and 2.5 acre playing field.
Our seven core values of kindness, curiosity, freedom, ambition, courage, community and joy, inform all that we do and how we behave as a school community. They guide our approach to teaching and learning, to pastoral care and to wellbeing, and our engagement with those around us. We nurture our pupils both academically and pastorally, enabling them to be happy, confident and inquisitive children. Through a broad range of subjects, inspiring teaching and plenty of exciting activities, we ensure that our school is a really fun place to be where curiosity is stimulated, and a love of learning is encouraged. Above all, we are a kind, friendly and joyful school.
Our Year 6 leavers go onto the leading independent and Grammar schools in London and Kent, achieving outstanding results and scholarship offers. Read more about our outstanding 2025 leavers’ results here.

A warm welcome to the Alumni association of Blackheath Prep
In 2023, in celebration of 35 years of Blackheath Prep, and commemorating 200 years of a school on our site, we launched the Blackheath Prep Alumni association.
Keep In Touch
Are you a former pupil, parent or staff member of Blackheath Prep? If so, we would be delighted to hear from you.
The Blackheath Prep alumni association is a great way to reconnect with old friends and colleagues, keep in touch with the latest news from Blackheath Prep, and perhaps even share your expertise and skills with a new generation of Blackheath Prep pupils as a visiting speaker or mentor.
Once registered, Alumni will receive newsletters and invitations to special events, including an annual alumni reunion event.
Be part of the Blackheath Prep community!
Tell us your news!
We are keen to hear from former Blackheath Prep pupils and find out where you are now. Do share your news and let us know your study and career choices since leaving Blackheath Prep.
Email us at alumni@blackheathprep.co.uk.
Share your memories
Do you have memories of your time at Blackheath Prep that you would like to share? A favourite teacher? Or a memorable school trip?
We would love to hear from you.
Spread the word
If you are in touch with parents and pupils who have a connection to Blackheath Prep, please help us spread the word and let them know about the alumni association.
Gallery
View photos of Blackheath Prep, past and present, on our Gallery page.
Keep it social
You can follow the Blackheath Prep social accounts for daily insights into life for our current Blackheath Prep pupils.
Contact Us
If you would like to get in touch, please email alumni@blackheathprep.co.uk

Eltham College Family of Schools
Blackheath Prep is part of the Eltham College Family of Schools incorporating Eltham College, Eltham College Junior School and Blackheath Prep. While each school retains its own distinct individual identity and Heads, the family of schools share an educational vision, ethos and values.
For Blackheath Prep pupils who select Eltham College as their senior school of choice we offer the benefit of a preferential application process which enables our pupils to sit an early entrance exam for Eltham College at the start of Year 6. Places and scholarships (where applicable) at Eltham College are then offered to successful pupils ahead of external candidates. On acceptance of the offer, pupils can then withdraw from the 11+ cycle.
In the summer term of Year 6, Blackheath Prep pupils will join their peers from Eltham College Junior School to attend special lessons at Eltham College to prepare them for their move to senior school.
Places offered via the preferential application process are subject to Eltham College’s usual entry requirements.
Find out more about the application process – Eltham College Admissions Infographic.

Meet the Head
A warm welcome to Blackheath Prep, a happy and thriving co-educational prep school for children aged 3 to 11. We are located in an idyllic setting on the edge of the heath close to Blackheath Village and our five-acre site offers superb specialist facilities, large playgrounds, forest school areas and extensive playing fields.
At Blackheath Prep, we seek to offer an education without boundaries and strive to ensure that every child shines and reaches their full potential. We unlock confidence, excitement, fresh thinking and a sense of fun and adventure in the full belief there are no limits to what each child can achieve.
We are committed to achieving academic excellence within an ethos of strong pastoral care and supported by a rich and varied co-curricular programme. We aim to help children develop the courage to believe in themselves, to take risks, to try new things, to be bold, brave, resilient and tenacious. We encourage everyone to learn from mistakes and rise to challenges.
Community is at the heart of our school. We believe strongly that children thrive when they are happy and nurtured and so it is no surprise that visitors comment on our warm atmosphere and our culture of kindness.
Our teachers work hard to ensure that life for the children within our care is stimulating, exciting and joyful. We aim to spark children’s natural curiosity for the world, leading them to discover, to wonder and to dare to go further. And we aim to give children the freedom to grow, to explore and to exceed their own expectations and ours. Each year our Year 6 pupils achieve outstanding results in their senior school transfers, moving on to the leading schools in London and Kent. Read more about our leavers’ results here.
It is a great privilege and responsibility to be involved in educating and shaping the lives of young people. At Blackheath Prep, we take our role very seriously. If you are considering the school, I hope this website will give you a flavour of our ethos and what we stand for.
Regular open mornings are held throughout the term and I encourage you to visit us and experience our warm welcome at first hand.
Thank you for your interest in our school and I very much look forward to meeting you in the future.
About
Vikki Lloyd (formerly Meier) joined Blackheath Prep as Head in September 2025. She was previously at Eltham College which she joined in 2016, first as Deputy Head of the Junior School, before being appointed Head of the Junior School in 2020. Vikki read Anthropology at Durham University, and has an MA in Educational Policy and Practice from the University of London, where she also gained her PGCE.

The Pre-Prep area of the school warmly welcomes pupils moving up from our Nursery and covers Reception to Year 2. We pride ourselves on our family ethos and we believe in knowing each and every child as an individual in order to nurture them and celebrate their strengths, as well as supporting them to be the very best they can be.
Watch a video with Claire Wates, Head of Pre-Prep to find out more.
We don’t have a 4+ intake into Reception, but occasionally places become available in the Pre-Preps. Please contact our Admission Office on 020 8305 5062 for details, or register your child for an occasional vacancy here.
Our primary aim is to provide a safe, happy and stimulating environment in which children can flourish to their full potential and build the foundations for a love of learning. We encourage a sense of independence, right from the Early Years Foundation Stage, to instil confidence and to develop social skills, as well as inspiring the children to explore and question the world. We also aim to enable our children to begin to develop attitudes and values which will lead them to become happy and responsible adults. Our pupils strive for high standards, both inside and outside the classroom, take pride in their achievements and enjoy participating wholeheartedly in the life of the school.
During the day, you will hear the corridors ringing with the sounds of music, tapping feet in the dance class, excited chatter, laughter and singing, or the class teacher sharing their favourite story with the children.
Each class has its own qualified teacher and at least one teaching assistant. Our staff are highly qualified and dedicated professionals who have an excellent understanding of how children learn and thrive in a developmental, child-centred way.
We warmly invite you to come and see us in action and learn more about the exceptional learning experiences we offer.
Claire Wates HEAD OF PRE PREP

Prep
As children move into Year 3, their journey at the Prep begins. They are prepared for the transition with a focus on independence and building confidence. Additional places for Year 3 sometimes arise and pupils are assessed during our 7+ assessment day.
We have two Prep forms per year group, each with their own form teacher. Lessons are taught increasingly by specialist teachers, with Form teachers assuming responsibility for the pastoral care of their pupils. In Years 3 and 4, teachers are also supported by teaching assistants.
Our focus remains on developing a sound knowledge base, curiosity and the ability to think critically. Pupils are encouraged to become inquisitive and independent learners and to make the most of every opportunity provided through the broad and varied subject areas and the range of facilities and resources on offer.
Blackheath Prep pupils achieve outstanding results in senior school entrance exams for both the maintained and the independent sectors, and also excel in Academic, Music, Drama, Art and Sport scholarship offers. The preparation they receive is well structured and responds to the needs of individual pupils. Advice and support is provided for parents during the secondary school transfer process and pupils leave Blackheath Prep well-prepared to meet the challenges of their secondary education. Read more about this year’s superb offers here.
As part of the Eltham College Family of Schools, our pupils also benefit from a priority places scheme, enabling them to sit the entrance exam in the September of Year 6 ahead of external candidates if they select Eltham College as their senior school of choice.
To find out more about available places, and details of what a Blackheath Prep education can offer your child contact our Admissions Office on 020 8305 5062.

Drama
At Blackheath Prep, all children from Nursery upwards receive weekly timetabled Drama lessons. Drama is taught by specialist teachers, each with a background in professional theatre.
Initially, we focus children’s raw energy into organised and structured drama, encouraging them to engage with characters and roles using improvisation, mime and storytelling. Children learn to express themselves in a clear and considered manner, working on articulation and diction as well as clarity of movement. They also learn to view their work from the perspective of an audience and to practise constructive criticism.
By Year 6, we aim for children to be able to create and perform effective pieces of drama using a variety of skills and techniques.
During the school year, pupils of all ages perform to a wider audience in our school assemblies, productions and concerts. In pupils’ final term in Year 6, a major production takes place that combines work from Music, Drama and Dance.
We are proud to be able to offer such exciting opportunities to our children to develop their confidence and self-esteem through drama. It is inspiring to see them demonstrate such creativity and courage as they progress through the school.

Open Days & Tours
Visiting a school is an important part of the decision-making process for families who are shortlisting schools for admissions applications. Families are warmly encouraged to visit Blackheath Prep to meet the Head, teaching staff and Admissions team, and enjoy a tour of our school and facilities to get a sense of what it is like to be part of the Blackheath Prep community.
We offer two key opportunities to visit: our Saturday Family Open Days, held twice a year, and our regular Group Tours. Full details are below. Please note that spaces at both Open Days and Group Tours are limited and early booking is highly recommended.
*Applications are now open for Nursery entry in September (closing date: Friday 16 October 2026), as well as for Prep (7+ and occasional vacancies). We also have very limited availability in Years 3 & 4. Find out more.
Open Days
We hold a Saturday Open Day in both the Autumn and Summer terms for prospective families. Parents and children will have the opportunity to hear our Head talk about the school, meet staff, pupils and our Parents’ Association, as well as tour our extensive grounds and see the academic and co-curricular facilities.
Group Tours
Tuesday mornings 9.15am – 10.45amWe offer group tours of the school for prospective parents once a month during term-time. These tours provide an opportunity to visit us on a working school day, and to ask questions about the school and our admissions process prior to or after registering your child. During the visit there will be a short presentation from a member of the senior leadership team before a guided tour to experience the whole school at work, from Nursery through to Year 6.
These tours are for parents and carers only. During the Autumn term, places on Tuesday tours are only available to parents who are applying for a place in the next 3+ and 7+ intake, or for occasional vacancies where places are available.
Virtual Tour
Take a virtual tour around the school with our interactive map to view 360 degree photos of the school and facilities, and watch videos from our Head and Senior Leadership Team.

Art & Design
Inspiring creativity and developing children’s observation and awareness of the world around them is fundamental to their spiritual, cultural and social development and wellbeing.
Our art curriculum is designed with experimentation and progression of skills at its forefront, engaging each child to build confidence in their own creative ability. Children enjoy a wealth of opportunities to develop their curiosity, resilience and self-expression.
Pupils are introduced to the core art elements and explore an exciting range of skills and techniques, from drawing and painting to wire sculpture and ceramics. Weekly specialist Art teaching and technical support helps each child reach their full potential as an artist.
Our art facilities are exceptional and children create their marvellous art in a busy yet relaxed atmosphere. They are free to express their individuality, working independently as well as in groups and on larger scale collaborative projects.
We inspire a joyful exploration of media, allowing children the freedom to take risks and to find their own ways of working whilst enhancing their technical skills, knowledge and understanding of media and core elements.
We celebrate our children’s amazing achievements by displaying artwork around the school. We also exhibit at our own Annual Summer exhibition and at external exhibitions.

English
At Blackheath Prep, we aim to foster a lifelong love of language and literature through our creative English curriculum, which is deeply enriched to engage, excite, inspire and challenge our pupils.
Our children are immersed in a rich reading culture, sparking a joy in reading from an early age and nurturing our pupils to become fluent, confident and passionate readers and writers.
From Reception to Year 2, children develop their early reading and language skills through our Systematic Synthetic Phonics programme which provides exciting opportunities to learn through tactile resources, visual prompts, nursery rhymes, songs, stories, games and interactive ICT.
In the Pre-Prep, children are taught English by their form teachers, but as they progress from Year 3 onwards English is increasingly taught by specialist subject teachers.
Creative writing is taught through the use of high-quality texts, inspiring stimulus and engaging experiences that ‘hook’ and excite the children. Children are taught to write for a clear purpose (writing to entertain, inform, persuade or debate) and audience, including opportunities to publish, perform and present. In addition, we provide author visits, poetry workshops, literary competitions, book festivals and library trips.
We have a beautiful, well-stocked library housed in the school’s former chapel, with a study area for research and a cosy area where children can curl up to enjoy a good read. Pupils also have access to well-stocked book corners in every classroom.

Geography
All children are naturally curious about the world around them. Our Geography teaching at Blackheath Prep aims to capture that curiosity and inspire children to develop a sense of wonder in – and a sense of responsibility towards – the wonderful world around them.
Through stimulating lessons, children are introduced to the diversity of people and places in the world. Children are encouraged to ask questions and to reflect on their own experiences and that of others and also on the physical environment close to home and further away.
Global issues such as deforestation of the Amazon rainforest and climate change are introduced so that children begin to understand the effect of human activity on the environment and develop an awareness of sustainable development.
The Geography curriculum aims to equip children with investigative skills and problem-solving capabilities. Fieldwork techniques using a range of resources and equipment are developed at school, in the local environment and on field trips to local environmental centres. Often, children are encouraged to take positive action through class-based projects and whole school initiatives.
The future of our world is in the hands of our children. We aim to make those hands capable and careful hands that value their responsibility.
